CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with history of recurrent kidney stones; follow-up of hypertension and diabetes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports pain from kidney stone that has been intermittent. She presented to the emergency room last week. She believes the stone passed approximately three days ago. She denies current hematuria and denies current pain. She has a history of approximately 7-8 kidney stones. She reports being given pain medication (Percocet) at the hospital. She has not seen a urologist in approximately one year but has been seen by one previously.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Patient reports occasional insomnia with worry as a trigger. She has tried meditation apps which help. She has tried melatonin a couple of times with minimal benefit. She denies wanting to take sleeping pills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension. Diabetes mellitus type 2 (diagnosed approximately one year ago). Recurrent kidney stones. Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (known, unchanged). Insomnia.

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Metformin 500 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports difficulty avoiding fast food due to being on the go. Admits to consuming cakes and cookies. She has difficulty finding time to prepare food. She sleeps with television on and keeps phone by bedside. She does not regularly check blood glucose.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles. Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, unchanged from prior. Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation. Costovertebral angle: No tenderness on right side.

RESULTS
Home blood pressure readings: 130-140 systolic over 60-70 diastolic (noted improvement from initial reading of approximately 180 systolic). Last A1C: 6.7 (slightly elevated, improved from initial diagnosis one year ago).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stones: Patient has passed current stone. Will obtain urinalysis and urine culture. Referral to urology with Dr. Harris given recurrent kidney stones. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. No changes to current medication. Refills provided. Referral to nutrition consultation for dietary management, targeting sodium intake of 2300 mg or less daily. Diabetes mellitus type 2: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Patient instructed to check blood glucose before each meal. Insomnia: Prescribed Melatonin 10 mg as needed. Advised to practice sleep hygiene including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and using iPhone sleep mode if available. Follow-up appointment in three months.
